draft.title: Scientific notation for large numbers
card: Scientific notation writes a large number as a number from 1 to less than 10, times a power of 10. The power is positive.
To write 3 400 000: put the point after the first non-zero digit to get 3.4. Count how many places the point moved. It moved 6 places.
So 3 400 000 = 3.4 × 10⁶. The power of 10 is the number of places the point moved.
To go back, multiply by the power of 10. 10⁶ is 1 000 000, so 3.4 × 10⁶ = 3 400 000. A number such as 34 × 10⁵ is not in scientific notation, because 34 is not less than 10.
draft.remember: Large number: a number from 1 to less than 10, times 10 to a positive power.

a.q: Which is 52 000 000 written in scientific notation?
a.why: The point moves 7 places to give 5.2, so the power is 7. 5.2 × 10⁶ is tempting, but it counts only the 6 zeros and not the places the point moved.
a.clue: Count the places from the end of the number to after the 5.

b.q: A tank holds 7.8 × 10⁵ litres of water. How many litres is that?
b.why: 10⁵ is 100 000, and 7.8 × 100 000 = 780 000. The point moves 5 places to the right. 78 000 is tempting, but it moves the point only 4 places.
b.clue: Move the decimal point right by the same number of places as the power.
